theater: 巴拉那河下游與南巴拉圭

battle.name: 巴拉圭戰爭
battle.theater: 巴拉那河下游與南巴拉圭
battle.brief: 一八六四年十二月，巴西聯同阿根廷、烏拉圭組成三方聯盟向巴拉圭宣戰，在巴拉那河下游與南巴拉圭打了五年。巴拉圭獨力迎戰，以自產前裝野戰砲與內河艦隊死守亞松森與烏米塔要塞；聯軍以重砲攻壞要塞、以騎兵斷其退路，於一八七〇年三月一日塞羅科拉一役瓦解巴軍。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰方分成兩大集團：一方是南美洲的「三方聯盟」——巴西帝國、阿根廷邦聯與烏拉圭共和國；另一方是獨自作戰的巴拉圭共和國。巴西方面，維多利亞王朝以「解放軍」為主力，名義上由皇帝佩德羅二世統率，實際指揮權交給元帥路易斯·阿爾維斯·德利馬·伊西爾維拉（卡希亞斯公爵），一八六六年之後交由歐恩伯爵曼努埃爾·路易斯·奧索里奧率第二師；海軍由上將安東尼奧·路易斯·達席爾瓦·巴羅索統率，旗下有巡防艦、砲艦與內河砲艇，並以自製魚雷艇封鎖河道。阿根廷邦聯由總統巴托洛梅·米特雷領軍，恩特里奧斯省省長胡斯托·何塞·烏爾基薩以本省私兵組成騎兵師，是聯軍中唯一配備大量騎兵的部隊；烏拉圭由總統韋南西奧·弗洛雷斯指揮圍城部隊，並在拉普拉塔河口維持封鎖。巴拉圭方面，總統弗朗西斯科·索拉諾·洛佩斯一身兼任全軍最高統帥，軍隊按師、旅編制，兵員由民兵、徵召役與「老兵連」組成，全國按戶徵發銅鐵器物供應軍需；這支軍隊同時也是這個國家僅有的產業與財政支撐。
countriesEn: The opposing sides of this war fell into two groups: on one side the South American Triple Alliance of the Empire of Brazil, the Argentine Confederation and the Republic of Uruguay; on the other, the Republic of Paraguay, which fought alone. On the Brazilian side the Victorian monarchy fielded the Libertador Army as its main body, nominally under Emperor Pedro II, while real command passed to Marshal Luís Alves de Lima e Silva, Duke of Caxias, and from 1866 onward to Count d'Eu, Manuel Luís Osório, who led the Second Division; the navy was commanded by Admiral Antônio Luís da Silva Barroso, with corvettes, gunboats and river craft, and added home-built torpedo boats to seal the waterways. Argentina's Confederation fought under President Bartolomé Mitre, while Justo José de Urquiza, governor of Entre Ríos, raised a division from his own province's private troops, the only formation in the alliance built around large numbers of cavalry horses; Uruguay was represented by President Venancio Flores, who directed the besieging force and kept the blockade at the mouth of the Río de la Plata. On the Paraguayan side President Francisco Solano López was supreme commander in the same person as head of state; the army was organised into divisions and brigades, its ranks filled by militia, conscripts and companies of elderly men, while the state levied copper, iron and household goods from every family to feed the war effort, that army being at once the only industry and the only support the state still had.
people: 決定戰局的人物分屬兩邊。巴拉圭的靈魂是索拉諾·洛佩斯，這位以嚴酷手段維持專制的總統自任全軍最高統帥，屢次親率兵團作戰；他腳下的根據地是父親卡洛斯·洛佩斯總統留下的烏米塔兵工廠群，由德國工程師費德里科·威斯納與卡洛斯·羅埃德主持，使巴拉圭得以自造火藥、槍械與鑄鐵小砲。貝納迪諾·卡瓦列羅是巴拉圭騎兵的指揮官，一八六七年一月率八千餘騎衝擊聯軍第二師，折戟於聖安東尼奧與羅梅羅內一役，此役在巴方口中稱為「馬刺之戰」；一八六九年他在亞科斯塔尼烏的敗局中率殘部突圍。巴西這邊，卡希亞斯公爵以穩紮穩打的攻勢拿下庫魯帕伊蒂並圍困烏米塔，歐恩伯爵率第二師在巴西南境強行突破後方，兩人交替主持正面戰線；卡希亞斯在一八六七年秋一度卸下兵權，又於一八六九年出山指揮最後一段戰線。上將巴羅索在里阿丘河一役以十六艦對六艦，徹底封死巴拉圭的河流進口。阿根廷方面，烏爾基薩在帕翁戰役以騎兵總攻救回第一師，一八六七年三月底在瓜伊拉斯渡口強渡巴拉那河，一八六九年再率聯軍在亞科斯塔尼烏給巴軍致命一擊；烏拉圭的弗洛雷斯守住蒙得維的亞，封鎖線最終在洛佩斯陣亡當日完成合圍。
peopleEn: The people who decided the war came from both sides. The soul of the Paraguayan effort was Solano López, the president who held power by severity and who made himself commander-in-chief of the whole army, repeatedly leading his formations in person; the ground he stood on was the chain of foundries at Humaitá left behind by his father, President Carlos López, run by the German engineers Friedrich Wisner and Carlos von Roeder, which allowed Paraguay to manufacture its own powder, small arms and cast-iron cannon. Bernardino Caballero commanded the Paraguayan cavalry; in January 1867 he led more than eight thousand horsemen against the allied Second Division and was broken at San Antonio and San Bernardino, a battle the Paraguayans themselves called the Battle of the Spurs, and in the disaster at Acosta Ñu in 1869 he cut his way out with the remnants. On the Brazilian side the Duke of Caxias took Curupayty by a steady advance and then invested Humaitá, while Count d'Eu forced the far rear of the Paraguayan south with the Second Division, the two men taking turns directing the main front; Caxias laid down his command once in the autumn of 1867 and came back out in 1869 to lead the last phase of the campaign. Admiral Barroso, with sixteen ships against six at the Riachuelo, sealed the river and cut Paraguay off from the waterways. For Argentina, Urquiza's cavalry charge at Pavón saved the First Division; at the end of March 1867 he forced the Paraná at the Paso de las Guayras, and in 1869 he led the allied army to the decisive blow at Acosta Ñu. For Uruguay, Flores held Montevideo, and the blockade was closed on the very day López fell.
kits: 卡面這門一八五〇年的德製前裝線膛野戰砲，技術上代表的是普魯士砲兵在同一時期推動的線膛化：把前裝野戰砲的炮膛加長、在膛壁刻上膛線，讓同一份藥量把長形彈丸送得更遠，再配上銅或鋼製的密閉火室。它在本戰役中沒有以德國原裝出現，但同代設計正是兩軍野戰砲的共同母型。巴西的骨架砲以英國安菲爾德（Anfield）設計的六十磅與三十二磅前裝線膛長射程砲為主力，配以六磅、七磅滑膛野戰砲以及一批從舊軍械庫翻出的老砲；巴拉圭則完全依賴自製，烏米塔兵工廠以本地生鐵鑄造一、二、三、四、六磅乃至十二磅、二十四磅的小口徑野戰砲，數量以千計。火藥與彈藥是兩軍最吃緊的東西：巴西可以從歐洲與里約熱內盧輸入，聯軍的封鎖線卻切斷了巴拉圭的外購水路；一八六五年九月里阿丘河海戰之後，巴拉圭只剩亞松森下游的內河航線與陸路，長射程重砲射程再遠，缺彈也等於廢鐵。步槍方面，巴西以擊發式前裝步槍為主，多為舊式米納槍的改型；巴拉圭大量仿造南美常見的「帕塞拉」式步槍與獵槍，膛線與刺刀常因材料不足而簡化。馬匹是巴拉圭真正的優勢：全國牧場與畜群龐大，軍馬數量一度超過聯軍任何一師，一八六七年一月那場大規模騎兵衝鋒正是靠馬群衝量取勝；而一八六七至六八年的牛瘟與馬瘟，讓聯軍在後方損失難以統計的畜力，兩萬人的軍隊在雨季行軍數百公里後往往寸步難行。
kitsEn: The muzzle-loading field gun on this card, a German piece of 1850, represents technically the rifling programme the Prussian artillerymen pushed forward at the same time: lengthening the chamber of the muzzle-loader, cutting rifling into the bore so that the same charge of powder throws a longer projectile further, and fitting a copper or steel chambered piece. It did not appear in this war as a German original, but designs of its generation were the common ancestor of the field artillery on both sides. The backbone of the Brazilian artillery was the long-range sixty-pounder and thirty-two-pounder rifled muzzle-loaders of Charles Anfield's English design, supported by six- and seven-pounder smoothbore field guns and a batch of old pieces dug out of obsolete depots. Paraguay relied entirely on its own manufacture: the Humaitá foundries cast small-calibre field guns of one, two, three, four and six pounds up to twelve and twenty-four pounds from local pig iron, in numbers running into the thousands. Powder and ammunition were the tightest commodity of all: Brazil could import from Europe and from Rio de Janeiro, but the allied blockade cut off Paraguay's foreign purchases; after the naval battle of the Riachuelo in September 1865 Paraguay was left with the inland waterways below Asunción and with land routes only, and a long-range heavy gun without shells was so much scrap iron. As for small arms, the Brazilians used percussion muzzle-loading rifles, mostly conversions of old Minié rifles; Paraguay copied in bulk the Parseira-type rifles and shot guns common in southern South America, with rifling and bayonets often simplified for want of material. Horses were Paraguay's real strength: the country's pastures and herds were vast, its remounts at times outnumbered those of any single allied division, and the great mounted charge of January 1867 was won on the weight of horseflesh; but the cattle and horse plagues of 1867 and 1868 destroyed an unmeasurable amount of draught animal in the allied rear, and a division of twenty thousand men, after marching several hundred kilometres through the rains, could often go no further.
tactics: 聯軍的戰術是典型的一八六〇年代打法：先以炮兵與工程兵找殼，架起野戰砲與拆下來的艦砲，在遠距離上把守軍的立靶打成碎屑，再由工兵挖壕、填壕、搭浮橋，一段一段向前推。卡希亞斯公爵的公式是「從不冒險」：一八六六年八月攻擊庫魯帕伊蒂，他以三天的正面炮擊加側翼迂回拿下洛佩斯的野戰陣地，之後圍困烏米塔，卻在後方補給線上被拖住。一八六七年一月，歐恩伯爵率第二師在巴拉圭南境強行渡過巴拉那河，一月十六日至二十五日在聖安東尼奧、羅梅羅內與洛馬斯貝爾德一線與巴拉圭騎兵對峙：他用中空的方陣把人馬圈在刺刀與火槍之間，等對方衝進射程再以整齊射擊收穫騎兵，加特林機關砲也投入了正面射擊。烏爾基薩走的是另一條路：一八六七年三月底他以一萬餘人與浮橋在瓜伊拉斯渡口強渡，橋斷時仍損失一千多人；此後用恩特里奧斯與科連特斯的騎兵沿內陸迂迴，切斷亞松森與南部各省的聯繫，逼迫洛佩斯分兵。巴拉圭的戰術則是集中兵力死守要點：洛佩斯在聖佩德羅附近構築庫魯帕伊蒂的塹壕與砲壘，在一八六六年五月的圖尤蒂之役中以集中砲火擊潰米特雷的正面攻擊；但他的騎兵一旦離開掩體進入平原，就會撞上聯軍的方陣與刺刀牆，而他的補給線依賴脆弱的內河航運，一次里阿丘河的封鎖就足以讓他無法從歐洲補充長射程砲彈。
tacticsEn: The allies fought with the standard method of the 1860s: first the artillery and engineers went in to find the shell, emplacing field guns and ship guns removed from their mounts so that at long range they broke the defenders' standing targets into splinters, and then the engineers dug, filled and bridged, pushing forward section by section. The Duke of Caxias had a formula, never to take risks: when he attacked Curupayty in August 1866 he used three days of frontal bombardment combined with a flanking movement to take López's field position, and afterwards he invested Humaitá and was pinned there by the length of his own supply line. In January 1867 Count d'Eu forced the Paraná in the far south of Paraguay, and between 16 and 25 January, at San Antonio, San Bernardino and Lomas Verdes, he met the Paraguayan cavalry: he closed his troops into a hollow square ringed by bayonets and muskets and waited for the horsemen to come into range before delivering volley after volley; Gatling guns were used there too, firing to the front. Urquiza took a different road: at the end of March 1867 he crossed the Paraná at the Paso de las Guayras with more than ten thousand men and pontoon bridges, and still lost over a thousand men when the bridge broke; afterwards his Entre Ríos and Corrientes cavalry rode inland in a wide arc, cutting the link between Asunción and the southern provinces and forcing López to divide his forces. Paraguay's own method was to concentrate on fixed points and hold: López built trenches and batteries around Curupayty near San Pedro and, at the battle of Tuyuti in May 1866, broke Mitre's frontal attack with concentrated gun fire; but his cavalry, once it left cover and reached open ground, ran into allied squares and walls of bayonets, and his supply line hung on a fragile inland navigation, so that a single blockade on the Riachuelo was enough to stop him from replacing the shells of his long-range guns.
data: 人口與兵力的比例最能說明這場戰爭的殘酷。巴拉圭一八六四年全國人口約三十五萬至四十萬，能上戰場的武裝人員約三萬至四萬人，約等於每十個國民就有一人握槍；戰爭最高峰時洛佩斯麾下集結的軍隊約五萬至六萬人。巴西靠一八六五年的《祖國志願軍法》募得三萬六千人，加上一八六四年組成的解放軍，最高峰時巴西投入約十萬人，阿根廷與烏拉圭再加數萬人，聯軍同時在戰線上約十三萬至十五萬。里阿丘河海戰是一個清楚對比：巴西十六艦對巴拉圭六艦，巴拉圭的兩艘巡防艦被俘，約一千五百人死傷被俘，巴西只損失數十人，無一艦沉沒。陸戰數字同樣刺眼：一八六六年五月二十四日圖尤蒂之役，米特雷以約一萬四千人、二十八門砲正面進攻，慘敗，折損約四千人、遺失火炮二十餘門；八月一日至三日庫魯帕伊蒂之役，第一師以約一萬人、五十門上下火炮攻破巴軍，宣稱斬首約一千五百人、俘虜六百餘人；九月一日帕翁之役，烏爾基薩的騎兵總攻擊潰巴軍右翼；一八六七年一月十六日至二十五日的「馬刺之戰」，巴軍出動八千至一萬騎攻擊第二師方陣，損失約兩千人、遺失火砲十餘門，聯軍損失數百人。圍城戰更耗時間：烏米塔要塞防線綿延約八公里，配置超過一百門砲，守軍約四千人，一八六七年六月三日投降；九月皮克西里一役，第二師約一萬二千人用八天炮擊再強攻，宣稱俘虜一千二百人。戰線縱深逾一千公里，聯軍後方基地距前線同樣超過一千公里；最後一役是一八七〇年三月一日的塞羅科拉，聯軍總兵力逾兩萬人圍攻不足三千人的巴軍殘部，洛佩斯在陣中陣亡。
dataEn: The ratio of population to men in arms shows how brutal this war was. Paraguay counted roughly three hundred and fifty to four hundred thousand inhabitants in 1864, with some thirty to forty thousand men armed and ready to fight, about one in every ten citizens; at the high point of the war López had perhaps fifty to sixty thousand men under his command. Brazil raised thirty-six thousand volunteers under the Volunteer Army of the Fatherland law of 1865, on top of the Libertador Army organised in 1864, and at its peak put about a hundred thousand Brazilian troops into the field, with tens of thousands more from Argentina and Uruguay, giving the allies something between one hundred and thirty and one hundred and fifty thousand men on the line at once. The battle of the Riachuelo shows the contrast clearly: sixteen Brazilian ships against six Paraguayan ones, two Paraguayan corvettes captured, some fifteen hundred men killed, wounded or taken prisoner, while Brazil lost only a few dozen men and not a single vessel. The figures on land are just as sharp: on 24 May 1866 at Tuyuti, Mitre attacked frontally with about fourteen thousand men and twenty-eight guns and was destroyed, losing some four thousand men and more than twenty guns; between 1 and 3 August at Curupayty the First Division broke the Paraguayan position with about ten thousand men and fifty-odd guns, claiming fifteen hundred dead, more than six hundred prisoners and several guns taken; on 1 September at Pavón Urquiza's cavalry charge turned the Paraguayan flank; and between 16 and 25 January 1867, in the Battle of the Spurs, eight to ten thousand Paraguayan horsemen charged the square of the Second Division and lost about two thousand men and more than ten guns, the allies losing a few hundred. Besieges took even longer: the defences of Humaitá ran for roughly eight kilometres, mounted over a hundred guns, and its garrison of about four thousand men capitulated on 3 June 1867; at Pikysyry in September the Second Division, some twelve thousand strong, bombarded for eight days and then assaulted, claiming twelve hundred prisoners. The front was over a thousand kilometres deep, and the allied bases lay just as far behind it; the last action was at Cerro Corá on 1 March 1870, where more than twenty thousand allied men surrounded fewer than three thousand Paraguayans and López was killed in the fighting.
cause: 戰爭不是突然爆發的，它有一條從一八五〇年代拖到一八六〇年代的引線。核心是巴拉圭與巴西在巴拉那河上游「伊瓜雷—科爾普斯」一段的邊界爭議：一八五二年的《巴拉那河條約》劃定了大致界線，隨後成立的混合委員會由巴西、巴拉圭與第三方代表組成，卻在最具爭議的伊瓜雷河與周邊島嶼上僵持不下。巴西主張並在一八六一至六二年出兵佔領馬爾薩爾島一帶的爭議區，巴拉圭認為那是侵略，兩國於一八六二年斷絕外交。另一層是航道與關稅：巴拉圭不承認巴拉那河對下游船隻自由通航，反對布宜諾斯艾利斯對過境貨物抽稅，直接牴觸布宜諾斯艾利斯與巴西的經濟利益；聯盟內部的阿根廷邦聯本身也面臨各省割據，烏拉圭的內戰則在桑托斯與蒙得維的亞兩端拉開戰線。同時，巴拉圭的洛佩斯政權並不打算讓步：國家拒絕外國軍艦進入內河，也拒絕接受仲裁，執意以自造兵備支撐與巴西的長期對抗。直接導火線是一八六四年十一月十二日，巴拉圭軍在亞松森港登船扣押巴西商船「侯爵·奧林達」號，船上還有巴西派駐的使節；十一月又有另一艘巴西船被扣。巴西的內閣在佩德羅二世的支持下下定決心，十一月三十日提出最後通牒，十二月十二日正式宣戰，聯盟另外兩國隨即以不同方式加入。
causeEn: The war did not break out suddenly; it had a fuse running back from the 1850s into the 1860s. At its core lay the boundary dispute between Paraguay and Brazil along the stretch of the upper Paraná known as the Igureí-Corpus: the 1852 Treaty of the Paraná fixed a rough line, and the mixed commission that followed, with delegates from Brazil, Paraguay and third parties, deadlocked over the most disputed stretch, the Igureí river and the islands around it. Brazil claimed the area and in 1861 and 1862 sent troops to occupy the disputed zone around Ilha de Marçal; Paraguay called this an aggression, and the two countries broke off diplomatic relations in 1862. A second layer was navigation and tariffs: Paraguay would not admit free navigation of the Paraná for shipping from downstream and opposed the dues Buenos Aires levied on cargo in transit, which cut directly into the commercial interests of Buenos Aires and Brazil; the Argentine Confederation inside the alliance was itself torn by provincial particularism, and the civil war in Uruguay stretched from one end to the other at Santos and Montevideo. At the same time López's Paraguayan government was not prepared to give way: the state refused foreign warships on its rivers and refused arbitration, insisting on supporting a long contest with Brazil with its own manufactured armament. The immediate trigger came on 12 November 1864, when Paraguayan troops boarded the Brazilian merchant steamer Marquês de Olinda in the port of Asunción and seized her, with the Brazilian envoy still aboard; another Brazilian vessel was taken later that month. The Brazilian cabinet, with the Emperor's backing, made up its mind, delivered an ultimatum on 30 November, and declared war on 12 December; the other two allies then entered in their own ways.
impact: 這場戰爭把巴拉圭的國家機器連根拔起。戰後巴國財政枯竭，中央銀行停止兌付，貨幣信用崩潰，一八六六年後大量印發無準備金的紙幣；興建中的鐵路、內河船隊、伊比庫伊的煉鐵爐與烏米塔兵工廠在戰火中拆毀，機器多被聯軍當作戰利品運走，工礦復原的設想至少延誤半個世紀。聯軍索取賠償與割地，最終以一八七六年的和約與邊界條約落實，巴拉圭把西部大片有爭議的土地交給巴西，把查科地帶割予玻利維亞。巴西則收穫甚豐：帝國軍隊的士氣與聲望推到頂點，佩德羅二世一八六六年訪英時受到的隆重接待即是明證，這支部隊此後成為共和時期仲裁政局與調解省際爭端的力量；巴西也藉此把勢力伸進亞馬遜上游的馬托格羅索，把國家邊界從中部推向西北，草原各省的財政與交通都因此重排。對阿根廷而言，烏爾基薩憑帕翁與瓜伊拉斯兩役的軍功坐穩聯軍騎兵統帥的地位，成為下一任國家領袖；聯軍內部聯邦派與布宜諾斯艾利斯派的裂痕也由此顯現，國家統一的路線直到十九世紀末才完成。對烏拉圭，弗洛雷斯贏得蒙得維的亞，長達十九年的白紅內戰告一段落。技術面上，這場戰爭留下兩個常被引用的先例：一八六六年三月十一日巴西魚雷艇在里阿丘河擊沉巴拉圭砲艇，被視為自航魚雷首次投入實戰；加特林機關砲也在南美戰場現身，開始進入各國的軍購清單。
impactEn: The war tore the Paraguayan state apparatus out by the roots. After it the treasury was empty, the central bank stopped paying out, the currency collapsed, and from 1866 a flood of paper money was issued without reserves; the railways under construction, the river fleet, the Ibicuí ironworks and the Humaitá foundries were torn down in the fighting and much of the machinery was carried off by the allies as booty, putting the recovery of industry and mining back by at least half a century. The allies demanded reparations and territory, and these were settled in the peace and boundary treaties of 1876: Paraguay handed the large disputed tracts in the west to Brazil and ceded the Chaco to Bolivia. Brazil gained the most. The morale and prestige of the imperial army reached their height, and the reception given to the Emperor during his state visit to Britain in 1866 showed it plainly; that army then became the arbiter of politics and the mediator of provincial disputes in the republican years. Brazil also pushed its influence up the Amazon into Mato Grosso, moved the national frontier from the centre towards the north-west, and reordered the finances and communications of the grassland provinces. For Argentina, Urquiza's standing with the allied cavalry rested on Pavón and the Guayras crossing, and he became the next head of the country; the fault line between the federalists and the Buenos Aires party inside the alliance showed itself here, and the unification of the country was not completed until the end of the nineteenth century. For Uruguay, Flores took Montevideo and the nineteen-year war between the Blancos and the Colorados was brought to a close. On the technical side the war left two much-cited precedents: on 11 March 1866 Brazilian torpedo boats sank a Paraguayan gunboat on the Riachuelo, regarded as the first combat use of self-propelled torpedoes, and the Gatling gun also appeared on a South American battlefield, entering the shopping lists of armies across the region.
result: 一八七〇年三月一日，洛佩斯在塞羅科拉被聯軍合圍，拒绝投降，在率騎兵反擊時陣亡；殘部在山崗上抵抗了數日，聯軍隨後控制亞松森，巴拉圭全國的抵抗在四月初大致平定。聯軍在亞松森組成以米特雷為首的共和三頭政治，一八七〇年通過的共和憲章規定廢除奴隸制度、承認西班牙語與瓜拉尼語並列，但這部憲法在本土從未真正實行，實權掌握在佔領當局與少數將領手中。兵器層面的結果更直白：烏米塔與皮克西里的砲兵被拆毀或運走，巴拉圭海軍殘餘的六艘船在下游窄口被聯軍封死，艇員於一八六九年自行鑿沉，國防工業再無重建可能；巴國常備軍被解散，只留下數千人的國民警衛隊，並禁止個人持有槍械。一八七六年，巴拉圭先後與巴西、阿根廷、烏拉圭以及玻利維亞達成和約與劃界條約，確認對巴拉那河與拉普拉塔河的航行權；邊界委員會在十九世紀七十年代末完成勘界，邊界線沿陸地自北至南貫穿，形成今日巴拉圭的疆域。戰爭的實際贏家是巴西聯軍：這場勝利把聯盟內部的權力天平推向巴西，也把巴拉圭從區域棋盤上抹去；而對巴拉圭來說，雖然損失慘重，國家並未被瓜分，仍以主權國的身份延續下來，只是軍力、財力與工業基礎都得從零開始重建。
resultEn: On 1 March 1870 López was surrounded at Cerro Corá, refused to surrender and was killed while leading a mounted counter-attack; the remnants held out on the heights for several more days, the allies then took Asunción, and resistance across Paraguay was broadly crushed by the beginning of April. The allies set up a republican triumvirate in Asunción headed by Mitre, and the republican charter drawn up in 1870 abolished slavery and gave Spanish and Guaraní equal standing, but that constitution was never actually put into effect on Paraguayan soil; real power stayed in the hands of the occupying authorities and a handful of generals. The result at the level of weapons is plainer: the guns of Humaitá and Pikysyry were broken up or carried away, the last six Paraguayan vessels were sealed in the narrows downstream by the allies and their crews scuttled them in 1869, and the defence industry had no prospect of being rebuilt. The Paraguayan regular army was dissolved, leaving only a national guard of some thousands, and private ownership of firearms was forbidden. In 1876 Paraguay concluded peace and boundary agreements in turn with Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Bolivia, confirming free navigation of the Paraná and the Río de la Plata; the boundary commissions finished their survey in the late 1870s, and the line running north to south across the interior gave Paraguay the frontier it has today. In practice the winners were the Brazilian-led alliance: the victory tipped the balance of power inside the alliance towards Brazil and wiped Paraguay off the regional board. Yet Paraguay itself, despite the ruin, was not partitioned, and continued as a sovereign state; only its army, its finances and its industrial base all had to be rebuilt from nothing.
